title: Best Dictation Software (2026): Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android
summary: The best dictation software for Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android in 2026, compared on accuracy, price, and reach.
body_markdown:
Dictation stopped being a compromise. The models are accurate enough that talking is now faster than typing for most everyday writing, the good apps drop text into whatever is in front of you, and you can carry the same setup from your laptop to your phone. The hard part is not whether to use dictation software, it is which one, because "best" means different things depending on whether you care about raw accuracy, offline privacy, the lowest price, or specialized command control, and no single tool wins all of them. This is a ranked shortlist across Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android, with one clear reason for each pick and the free tools most people forget they already have.


**The short answer:** the best all-round dictation software in 2026 is Aqua Voice, for its accuracy and voice editing across Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android. Dragon Professional is best for specialized command and macro workflows, Superwhisper for fully offline use, and Wispr Flow for polished cloud dictation. Every Mac, PC, and iPhone also ships free built-in dictation worth trying first.


## First, the free tools you already have


**On Mac and iPhone** , Apple Dictation is built in. Turn it on in Settings (see[how to use dictation on a Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/how-to-use-dictation-on-mac) ), press the shortcut, and it types what you say in almost any text field, with on-device processing on Apple Silicon and modern iPhones so your voice stays local. macOS also includes Voice Control, a separate hands-free layer for clicking and navigating by voice, built for accessibility rather than fast writing.


**On Windows** , there are two. Windows voice typing (Win + H on Windows 10 and 11) transcribes in the cloud through Microsoft's speech service. Voice Access (Windows 11 22H2 and later) runs on-device and adds full hands-free control of the PC, not just dictation.


These, along with app-specific tools like[Google Docs voice typing](https://aquavoice.com/blog/google-docs-voice-typing) , are genuinely fine for short messages and quick notes, and free is a hard price to beat. The reason people still look past them is accuracy on real work and control over the text. General built-in models stumble on names, technical terms, and code, give you no custom vocabulary, and insert a finished block you then fix by hand. When 9to5Mac ran the same passage through Apple Dictation and Aqua Voice, they counted 17 errors versus 1. If the free baseline keeps sending you back to the keyboard to correct it, that is your cue to look at the paid picks below.


## What separates good dictation software


Four things decide it. Pick the tool that wins on the one you care about most.


- **Accuracy on hard words.** Everyday prose is a solved problem. The gap opens on names, jargon, medical or legal terms, and code. A tuned model plus a custom dictionary is what closes it.
- **Where transcription happens.** On-device (offline, private, no connection needed) versus cloud (heavier cleanup, needs a connection) is a real trade, not a footnote.
- **Live text versus record-then-insert.** Watching words appear as you speak, and fixing them by voice, is a different experience from waiting for a finished block to land.
- **Reach.** A system-wide layer works in every app and, ideally, on every device you own. A single-app tool dies at that app's window edge.


Match your answer to the picks below.


## 1. Aqua Voice, best overall


We build Aqua Voice, so read this as informed rather than neutral, and judge the checkable claims for yourself.


Aqua runs on its own proprietary speech model,[Avalon](https://aquavoice.com/avalon-api) , rather than a general build. At its debut on the OpenASR leaderboard in October 2025, Avalon ranked as the top proprietary model (it now sits sixth overall as newer open models have landed). On the AISpeak benchmark Aqua reports 97.3% accuracy, a self-reported figure, so weigh it as one data point, with the independent 9to5Mac test above as the outside read.


What makes it the default for most people is the combination the others split up. On desktop, Aqua shows text as you speak, with final words landing in about 450 milliseconds, and you fix mistakes by voice with Voice Edit Mode instead of reaching for the keyboard. It works system-wide, so the same layer covers your editor, browser, Slack, and email, and a custom dictionary teaches it the names and terms you actually use. It runs on[Mac](https://aquavoice.com/mac) ,[Windows](https://aquavoice.com/windows) ,[iPhone](https://aquavoice.com/ios) , and[Android](https://aquavoice.com/android) , so your setup follows you from desk to phone, and it has a SOC 2 Type II audit report, with GDPR and HIPAA compliance for teams that need it.


Pricing is $10 per month billed annually, with a free tier of 1,000 words so you can try it before paying. The[guide](https://aquavoice.com/guide) walks through setup. The[Android app](https://aquavoice.com/android) is available on[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.aquavoice.android) and is included in the same subscription.


## 2. Dragon Professional, best for specialized command and macro workflows


Dragon is the veteran, and for a specific audience it is still the answer. Dragon Professional v16 is Windows-only now (Nuance discontinued the Mac version back in 2018), and at the time of writing it is roughly a $699 one-time purchase rather than a subscription. What you get for that is deep custom commands and macros, mature vocabulary training, and workflows built for dictation-heavy professions like medical and legal. (Clinicians should also read our roundup of the[best medical dictation software](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-medical-dictation-software) , which covers Dragon Medical One.)


The trade-offs are the price, the Windows-only reach, and a setup that expects you to invest time. If you want a full command-and-control dictation system on a PC and you dictate for a living, Dragon earns its place. If you mostly want fast, accurate writing across your apps and devices without the upfront cost, the picks above and below fit better. Our[Aqua vs Dragon](https://aquavoice.com/vs/dragon) page and the[Dragon alternatives for Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/dragon-alternatives-for-mac) roundup go deeper for anyone leaving Dragon behind.


## 3. Superwhisper, best for offline and local processing


Superwhisper is the pick when your voice should never leave your machine. It downloads a speech model and runs it on-device, so dictation works with no internet connection and nothing is sent to a server. That is the whole appeal, and for sensitive material it is the right call. It is Mac-first, with newer and more limited Windows and iOS builds, and the models it runs are user-chosen local Whisper builds, which the vendor discloses openly.


The trade-offs are setup and consistency: you choose and download models, and accuracy scales with the model and the hardware you run it on. At the time of writing it offers a free tier on small local models, with Pro around $8.49 per month or a one-time lifetime license near $250, which is the draw for people who would rather pay once. If offline is your line in the sand, start here.


## 4. Wispr Flow, best for polished cloud dictation


Wispr Flow is a polished cloud option and, like Aqua Voice, covers Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android. It transcribes on its servers and runs an automatic cleanup pass that trims filler and tidies phrasing, which is genuinely useful for quick email and chat. Both Aqua and Wispr offer Android apps, so compare accuracy, price, and workflow rather than choosing on Android availability alone.


The catch is price and the cloud trade. At the time of writing it runs roughly $12 to $15 per month depending on billing, with no lifetime license, and because it is cloud-based it needs a connection and processes your audio on its servers. Wispr says it runs Canto, its own speech model, announced in September 2026. Our[Aqua vs Wispr Flow](https://aquavoice.com/vs/wispr-flow) page covers that head-to-head.


**A caution before you pay for a year:** check what long-time users say about Wispr Flow on X (formerly Twitter), where opinions are mixed. A recurring complaint is that the product feels really good during the free trial and distinctly worse once you are locked into an annual plan. Those are user reports rather than something we can measure from the outside, and plenty of people are happy with it, but it is a good reason to stay on the monthly plan for a few months before you commit to a full year.


## A note on transcribing recordings


If your real job is turning recorded audio into text (interviews, meetings, podcasts, voice memos) rather than typing by voice, that is a different category. Tools like Otter.ai for meeting notes, or MacWhisper, which openly runs OpenAI's Whisper models on your Mac for file transcription, fit that need better than any of the live-dictation picks above. Know which job you are solving before you buy.


## How to choose


By platform:


- **Mac:** start with Aqua Voice, and compare it against the free Apple Dictation you already have. For the full ranked list, see[the best AI dictation app for Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-ai-dictation-app-for-mac) .
- **Windows:** Aqua Voice for everyday writing, Dragon Professional if you need deep command macros. The full breakdown is in[the best AI dictation app for Windows](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-ai-dictation-app-for-windows) .
- **iPhone:** try the built-in iOS dictation first, then the[Aqua Voice iPhone app](https://aquavoice.com/ios) if you want the same accuracy and custom dictionary as on your computer. The full ranked list, including Google's free offline app, is in[the best speech to text apps for iPhone](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-speech-to-text-app-for-iphone) .
- **Android:** the[Aqua Voice Android app](https://aquavoice.com/android) works with your existing keyboard. Tap the Aqua button, speak, and insert text into the app you are using; the[Android roundup](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-speech-to-text-app-for-android) compares it with Gboard and the rest.


By need:


- **Best all-round:** Aqua Voice.
- **Offline or privacy first:** Superwhisper.
- **Specialized command and macro control:** Dragon Professional.
- **Polished cloud dictation:** Wispr Flow.
- **Transcribing recordings:** Otter.ai or MacWhisper.


Try the free tier of whichever one matches your top priority. The category is good enough now that the only real mistake is continuing to type when you would rather talk.


## Frequently asked questions


**What is the best dictation software in 2026?** For most people it is Aqua Voice, thanks to its accuracy and voice editing, working system-wide across Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android. Dragon Professional is best for specialized command and macro workflows on Windows, Superwhisper is the strongest offline pick, and Wispr Flow is a polished cloud option. Every Mac, PC, and iPhone also has capable free built-in dictation worth trying first.


**Is there free dictation software?** Yes. Macs and iPhones include Apple Dictation, and Windows includes voice typing (Win + H) and Voice Access, all free. They are worth trying before you pay, but they offer no custom vocabulary and stumble on names, jargon, and code, which is why many people upgrade to a tuned app.


**What is the most accurate dictation software?** Accuracy depends on the passage, but the tuned, purpose-built models now clearly beat the general built-in ones on hard words. In a 9to5Mac head-to-head on the same passage, Apple Dictation made 17 errors to Aqua Voice's 1. A custom dictionary that learns your names and terms is what closes the remaining gap.


**Does dictation software work on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android?** Some does and some does not. Built-in tools are tied to their platform. Aqua Voice and Wispr Flow both run on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android. Aqua covers all four with one account and subscription. Dragon Professional is Windows-only and Superwhisper is Mac-first. If you want one setup across your devices, check platform support before you buy.
